## Methods

Mice
Six- to twenty-week-old mice were used in all experiments. In each experiment, mice were age-matched and sex-matched. Both sexes were used in our experiments with similar results. As described previously 40, hCD20-TamCre animals 98 (donated by Dr. M. Shlomchik, University of Pittsburgh, PA) were intercrossed with mice carrying the rosa26-flox-STOP-YFP allele 99 (Jax mice strain 006148) generating mice in which YFP is expressed in B cells upon Cre activation. These mice were crossed with Ars/A1 41 (donated by Dr L. Wysocki, National Jewish Health, CO) and MD4 56 (Jax mice strain 002595) B cell antigen receptor transgenic mice to generate hCD20-TamCre x rosa26-flox-STOP-YFP x Ars/A1 mice and hCD20-TamCre x rosa26-flox-STOP-YFP x MD4 mice, respectively. B cells from these mice will be referred to as WT Ars/A1 and WT MD4. To generate mice in which Lyn deletion can be induced in B cells, these mice were crossed with Lynflox/flox mice (donated by Dr. C. Lowell, UCSF, San Francisco, CA) 46. To generate mice in which SHIP-1 and Lyn haploinsufficiency can be induced in Ars/A1 B cells, these mice were crossed with previously described mice 40 in which SHIP-1 deletion can be induced in B cells (hCD20-TamCre x rosa26-flox-STOP-YFP x SHIP-1flox/flox x Ars/A1 mice). SHIP-1flox/flox mice were donated by Dr J. Ravetch (Rockefeller University, NY) In parallel, lines were generated that do not express a transgenic BCR to determine the effect of acute Lyn deletion in B cells from mice that express a WT repertoire of BCRs. Mice in which Lyn deficiency is constitutively restricted to the B cell lineage from early B cell development were generated by crossing Lynflox/flox mice with mb1cre mice 100 (Jax mice strain 020505). This line was crossed with Ars/A1 mice to generate mb1cre x Lynflox/flox x Ars/A1 mice. Lynflox/flox x Ars/A1 mice littermates were used as Lyn sufficient controls. In mb1cre mice the cre recombinase is inserted into the mb1 locus, which encodes CD79A, disrupting the expression of CD79A from that locus. To control for the impact of CD79A heterozygosity on the anergic phenotype we also crossed mb1cre mice with Ars/A1 mice and compared Ars/A1 littermates that did or did not contain the mb1cre construct.

In adoptive transfer experiments, C57BL/6J mice (Jax mice strain 000664) were used as recipients. For some of the signaling experiments, Ars/A1 and MD4 B cell antigen receptor transgenic mice were used without additional strains crossed in. At the end of each experiment the mice were euthanized by CO inhalation. Mice were housed and bred at the University of Colorado Denver Anschutz Medical Campus Vivarium (Aurora, CO) under ESPF conditions. C57BL/6J mice were purchased from Jackson Laboratories for experiments. All experiments with mice were performed in accordance with the regulations and with approval of the University of Colorado SOM Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee.

Tamoxifen treatments, adoptive transfers and immunizations.
Cre activity was induced by tamoxifen treatment. Tamoxifen (Sigma, T-5648) was dissolved in 10% ethanol (Decon Laboratories) and 90% corn oil (Sigma) at 20 mg/mL. In experiments in which we analyzed the impact of induced Lyn deletion on BCR signaling of splenic B cells, mice were injected once i.p. with 100 \u03bcL (2 mg) of tamoxifen/corn oil 7 days prior to analysis. Following a single tamoxifen injection we observed a deletion efficiency (measured as % YFP+ B cells) of 61.1 \u00b121.6%.

In adoptive transfer experiments in which we analyzed the impact of induced Lyn deletion on the ability of Ars/A1 B cells to maintain B cell tolerance, recipient mice were irradiated with 200 rads four hours prior to adoptive transfer to provide space for transferred cells as described previously 40. B cells from donor mice were enriched by depletion of CD43+ cells with anti-CD43-conjugated magnetic beads (CD43 (Ly-48), mouse; Miltenyi Biotec). Resultant populations were >97% B cells based on B220 staining and FACS analysis. Prior to transfer, donor B cells were labeled with CellTrace Violet Proliferation Kit, *for flow cytometry* (Invitrogen by Thermo Fisher) at 5 \u03bcM for 3 min at RT in complete medium (IMDM supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum (FCS), 1 mM Sodium Pyruvate, 2 mM L-Glutamine, 100 U/mL Pen/Strep, 50 \u00b5g/mL gentamicin and 0.1 mM 2-Me). The labeling was stopped by adding an excess of FCS, followed by 3 washes with Phosphate-Buffered Saline (PBS). 1-8x106 B cells in 200 \u03bcL PBS were adoptively transferred by i.v. injection. Twenty-four hours after transfer, Cre activity was induced by 100 \u03bcL (2 mg) tamoxifen injections i.p. on two consecutive days.

In experiments in which we analyzed the impact of induced Lyn deletion on the ability of MD4 B cells to mount an antibody response to Sheep Red Blood Cells-Hen Egg Lysozyme (SRBC-HEL) immunization, donor hCD20-TamCre x rosa26-flox-STOP-YFP x Lynflox/flox x MD4 mice and hCD20-TamCre x rosa26-flox-STOP-YFP x MD4 mice were injected i.p. with 100 \u03bcL (2 mg) of tamoxifen/corn oil. Six days post tamoxifen treatment, splenocytes were stained with B220-Alexa647 (clone RA3-6B2, Biolegend, 1:500) and B220+ YFP+ cells were sorted using a Beckman Coulter Astrios EQ cell sorter. 1.3x105 YFP+ B220+ cells were adoptively transferred by i.v. injection in 200 \u03bcL PBS into C57BL/6 recipient mice. Twenty-four hours post adoptive transfer the recipient mice were immunized by i.p. injection with 200 \u03bcL 1% SRBC-HEL. SRBC were purchased from the Colorado Serum Company and stored in sterile Alsever\u2019s solution at 4 \u00b0C. HEL was chemically coupled to SRBC. One mL packed SRBC was resuspended in 15 mL PBS containing 5 mg/mL HEL (Sigma). To cross-link, 1mL of 50 mg/mL 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide hydrochloride (Sigma) in PBS was added, mixed and incubated for 1 h at RT, with occasional mixing. Afterwards, the cells were washed four times in PBS and the conjugation of HEL to the SRBC cell surface was confirmed by flow cytometry after staining with Dylight650 conjugated anti-HEL (clone D1.3, produced and conjugated in house, 1:400). Five days post immunization splenocytes were harvested and analyzed for MD4 anti-HEL responses.

ELISPOT
For detection of IgMa Ars antibody secreting cells, microtiter plates were coated with 10 \u03bcg/mL Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA)-Ars or 10 \u03bcg/mL Ovalbumin (OVA)-Ars in PBS. For detection of IgMa MD4 antibody secreting cells, microtiter plates were coated with 10 \u03bcg/mL HEL in PBS. Before use, the plates were washed twice with PBS-0.05% Tween-20 and blocked with complete 10% FCS IMDM medium. Two-fold serial dilutions were made of splenic single cell suspensions starting at 1/50th of a spleen in the first well. The plates were incubated at 37\u00b0C at 7% CO2 overnight. MD4 and Ars/A1-derived antibody secreting cells were detected with Biotin-conjugated Mouse Anti-Mouse IgM[a] (Clone:DS-1; BD Biosciences, 1:2000), followed by Streptavidin-AP (SouthernBiotech, 1:2000). Between each step, the plates were washed 4 times with PBS-0.05% Tween-20. The plates were developed by incubating with ELISPOT development buffer (25 \u03bcM 5-bromo-chloro-3-indolyl phosphate p-toluidine, 100 mM NaCl, 100 mM Tris, 10 mM MgCl2 [pH 9.5]) for 1 h. The reaction was stopped by washing the plate once with double-distilled H2O. The number of spots at a cell dilution in the linear range was determined, and the number of antibody-secreting cells per spleen was calculated.

Flow cytometry
Single cell suspensions of splenic cells or bone marrow cells, flushed out of the two hindleg femurs, were prepared in 10% FCS complete medium, and red blood cells were lysed using Ammonium Chloride Potassium Lysis buffer (15 mM NH4Cl, 10 mM KHCO3, 0.1 mM Na2EDTA, pH 7.4). Cells were resuspended in PBS containing 1% BSA and 0.05% sodium azide and incubated with an optimal amount of directly fluorochrome labeled antibodies. Antibodies directed against the following molecules were used: B220-BV421 (clone RA3-6B2, Biolegend, 1:500), CD43-APC (clone S11, Biolegend, 1:200), CD69-BV786 (clone H1.2F3, BD Biosciences, 1:200), CD86-BV605 (clone GL1, BD Biosciences, 1:200), CD95-FITC (clone Jo2, BD Biosciences, 1:200), IgD-PE (clone 11-26c.2a, Biolegend, 1:300), and IgM (b-7-6, 1:200). b-7-6 was produced in our own laboratory and was directly conjugated to DyLight (Pierce/Thermo Scientific) fluorochromes, according to the manufacturer\u2019s protocol. The MD4 BCR was stained with its antigen HEL (Sigma) conjugated to Dylight 650 (Pierce/Thermo Scientific, 1:300) fluorophore, according to the manufacturer\u2019s protocol.

To determine the phenotype of Ars/A1 B cells following adoptive transfer, splenocytes were fixed and permeabilized with BD Cytofix/Cytoperm\u2122 and stained with Dylight650-E4 anti-Ars/A1 idiotype (E4 was produced and conjugated to DyLight\u2122 650 NHS Ester (Pierce/Thermo Scientific) in our laboratory, 1:300), Dylight488 anti-GFP (polyclonal Goat anti-GFP Antibody (600-101-215, Rockland) conjugated to DyLight\u2122 488 NHS Ester (Pierce/Thermo Scientific) in our laboratory, 1:500), and CD138-PE-Cy7 (Clone: 281-2; Biolegend, 1:300). Anti-GFP-Dylight488 was used to detect YFP in experiments in which we used fixatives that kill the fluorescence of YFP. The cells were washed twice, and events were collected on a CyAn ADP (Dakocytomation), a BD LSRFortessa\u2122 X-20 Cell Analyzer (BD Biosciences) or a Cytek Northern Lights (Cytek Biosciences) and analyzed using FlowJo software (Becton Dickinson & Company (BD). In all experiments, the same gating strategy was used. We gated on the lymphocyte population based on FSC/SSC properties but including larger cells to capture plasmablasts, followed by doublet exclusion, and gating on YFP+ E4+ events (Suppl Fig 13A). To calculate the absolute number of YFP+ Ars/A1 B cells per spleen in different states (undivided, proliferated and plasmablasts (proliferated and CD138+), we multiplied the total number of splenocytes (counted with a Beckman Coulter Vi-CELL) with the frequency of YFP+ E4+ events and the frequency of violet proliferation dyehi CD138lo (undivided), violet proliferation dyelo (proliferated), violet proliferation dyelo CD138hi (plasmablasts).

Analysis of BCR signaling by flow cytometry
To analyze protein phosphorylation by flow cytometry, splenocytes were resuspended in serum-free IMDM at a concentration of 107 cells/mL and incubated at 37\u02daC for 20-30 minutes prior to stimulation. In some experiments the PI3K inhibitor Ly294002 (Cell Signaling Technology), dissolved in DMSO, was added at 5 or 10 \u03bcM during the last 10 minutes of prewarming. Control tubes received DMSO only at an equal dilution. In some experiments the splenocytes were prestained with a Fab fragment of b-7-6 conjugated to Dylight 488 (1:250) at 4 \u02daC and washed twice with serum free IMDM prior to incubation at 37 \u02daC to allow for gating on subpopulations of B cells with equal IgM expression. B cells were stimulated with 10 \u03bcg/mL polyclonal F(ab\u2019)2 goat anti-mouse IgM (anti-\u03bc) (Jackson ImmunoResearch) or 5 \u03bcg/mL anti-IgDa (clone AMS 9.1, Santa Cruz Biotechnology) for the indicated time. Prior to stimulation with anti-IgDa the splenocytes were incubated with 10 \u03bcg/mL clone 2.4G2 to block binding to Fc\u03b3RIIB.

Signaling was stopped by adding formaldehyde (Tousimis) at a final concentration of 2%. If a methanol permeabilization method was used the cells were incubated at 37\u02daC for 10 min with the 2% formaldehyde. Afterwards the cells were spun down and resuspended in -80 \u02daC 100% MeOH (Fisher Scientific) and incubated on ice for 30 min. After permeabilization the cells were washed three times in PBS containing 1% BSA. Cell staining and washes were done in PBS/1% BSA. If BD Cytofix/Cytoperm permeabilization was used, the cells were immediately spun down following formaldehyde addition and resuspended in BD Cytofix/Cytoperm. The cells were incubated at 4 \u02daC for 20 minutes, followed by three washes with BD Perm/Wash buffer. Cell staining and washes were done in BD Perm/Wash buffer.

Methanol permeabilized cells were stained for: B220-BV421 (clone RA3-6B2 Biolegend, 1:500), Dylight488 anti-GFP (if cells express YFP, 1:500), pCD79A (pY182)-Alex647 (clone D189, Cell Signaling Technology, 1:50), pSyk (pY352)-Alex647 (Clone 17A/P-ZAP70, BD Biosciences, 1:5), pErk (pT202/pY204)-Alex647 (clone 20A, BD Biosciences, 1:5), pPLC\u03b32 (pY759)-Alex647 (clone K86-689.37, BD Biosciences, 1:5), pBLNK (pY84)-Alex647 (clone J117-1278, BD Biosciences, 1:5), Rabbit isotype control-Alex647 (Cell Signaling Technology, 1:200), mouse IgG1 isotype control-Alex647 (clone MOPC-21, BD Biosciences, 1:5). BD permeabilized cells were stained for: B220-BV421 (RA3-6B2 Biolegend, 1:500), Dylight488 anti-GFP (if cells express YFP, 1:500), pAkt (pS473)-Alex647 (clone M89-61, BD Biosciences, 1:5), I\u03baB\u03b1-Alex647 (clone L35A5, Cell Signaling Technology, 1:100), pS6 (pS235/pS236)-PE-Cy7 (clone cupk34k, eBioscience/Invitrogen, 1:100), Rabbit isotype control-Alex647 (Cell Signaling Technology, 1:200), mouse IgG1-Alexa647 isotype control (clone MOPC-21, BD Biosciences, 1:100) and mouse IgG1-PE-Cy7 isotype control (clone P3.6.2.8.1, eBioscience/Invitrogen, 1:200). The cells were stained for 1hr at RT and washed 3 times prior to analysis. Events were collected on a BD LSRFortessa\u2122 X-20 Cell Analyzer (BD Biosciences) or a Cytek Northern Lights (Cytek Biosciences) and analyzed using FlowJo software (Becton Dickinson & Company (BD). In all experiments, the same gating strategy was used. We gated on the lymphocyte population based on FSC/SSC properties, followed by doublet exclusion and gating on YFP+ B220+ events or B220+ events if the cells did not express YFP (Suppl Figs 4A, 5A and 6A).

Analysis of calcium mobilization
For measurements of intracellular free calcium concentration ([Ca2+]i), splenocytes (2*107/mL in IMDM medium containing 2% FCS) were simultaneously stained with anti-B220-Alexa647 (clone RA3-6B2 Biolegend, 1:500) and loaded with 5 \u03bcM Indo-1 acetoxymethyl (Indo1-AM) (Molecular Probes) for 30 min at RT. In some experiments 5 \u03bcM Ly294002 or b-7-6 Fab conjugated to Dylight 488 (1:250) was added. After washing once with IMDM with 2% FCS, the cells were resuspended at 107 cells/mL in warm IMDM with 2% FCS in a 500\u03bcL volume. Indo-1 was excited with a 355 nm laser, Ca2+-bound Indo-1 was detected using a 379/28 bandpass filter and unbound Indo-1 was detected using a 450/50-410LP bandpass filter. Relative free calcium concentration was determined by the ratio bound/unbound Indo-1. After the baseline was established by analysis for 30 seconds, cells were stimulated with 2-10 \u03bcg/mL F(ab\u2019)2 goat anti-mouse IgM (anti-\u03bc) (Jackson ImmunoResearch) or 5 \u03bcg/mL anti-IgDa (clone AMS 9.1, Santa Cruz Biotechnology) for 2 minutes. Prior to stimulation with anti-IgDa the splenocytes were incubated with 10 \u03bcg/mL clone 2.4G2 to block binding to Fc\u03b3RIIB. The bound/unbound Indo-1 ratio was measured using a BD LSRFortessa\u2122 X-20 Cell Analyzer (BD Biosciences) and analyzed using FlowJo software (Becton Dickinson & Company (BD). The area under the curve was calculated in FlowJo.

Immunoblotting
Splenic B cells were enriched by depletion of CD43+ cells with anti-CD43-conjugated magnetic beads (MACS anti-mouse CD43; Miltenyi Biotec). Resultant populations were >97% B cells based on B220 staining and FACS analysis. B cells were resuspended at 107/mL in serum-free IMDM and incubated at 37 \u02daC for 20-30 minutes. work presented. The only critique we identified was a concern that the presented work may have
a certain lack of novelty since Lyn has been extensively studied in the context of BCR signaling.
We would like to emphasize some key observations that we think are novel and significant,
which we think should be of interest to a larger audience.
As recognized by the reviewer, we think that linking Lyn function to B cell anergy is a
significant observation that is of interest to those studying immune tolerance and autoimmune
disease. It has puzzled the field that Lyn deficiency in two models of B cell anergy did not result
in a loss of B cell tolerance. Inhibitory receptors and phosphatases that are dependent on Lyn
function have been shown to be important for B cell anergy. Thus, one would expect a role for
Lyn in establishing and maintaining B cell anergy.
While we cannot say for certain why we observe a dependence of functional B cell anergy on
Lyn expression, while others have not, we suspect that two factors may contribute. The other
studies used classical Lyn knock out mice, while we use B cell restricted models. Dysregulation
of Lyn-deficient myeloid cells has an impact on Lyn-sufficient B cells (PMID: 23940344), which
may have confounding effects. Secondly, it is becoming apparent that B cell anergy exists on a
spectrum that uses several different mechanisms to obtain a sufficient level of unresponsiveness
to ensure B cell tolerance. We think that the Ars/A1 model used represents a subset of anergic B
cells in the wild type B cell repertoire that is dependent on Lyn function for functional anergy.
The second point that we think is of general interest relates to the mechanisms that an
autoreactive B cell can use to reduce the likelihood of productive antigen receptor signaling.
Downregulation of surface IgM is commonly used by autoreactive B cells. It is a characteristic of
anergic B cells, yet its impact on constraining downstream signaling and contributions to the
anergic signaling phenotype are not fully understood. Our data suggests that IgM antigen
receptor downregulation is responsible for most of the characteristic dampened signaling
previously described. However, anergic B cells use additional active suppressive mechanisms to
limit PI3K-dependent signaling. Our work demonstrates how multiple mechanisms contribute to
the overall suppressed phenotype of anergic B cells and it further emphasizes the importance of
regulation of PI3K signaling for B cell tolerance.

13) If F(ab’)2 fragments are used to prevent FcgRIIB recruitment, how is Lyn recruited to
dampen signaling in anergic B cells. Could this have something to do with ITAM
monophosphorylation of CD79A ITAMs in anergic B cells? How would this result change
with co-crosslinking of an ITIM containing protein.
These are excellent questions that we are actively investigating. Our working hypothesis is that
the preferential CD79A ITAM monophosphorylation observed in anergic B cells promotes
dampened downstream signaling in at least 3 ways. Monophosphorylated ITAMs do not recruit
Syk, limiting downstream activating signaling, but they can recruit Lyn. Lyn can phosphorylate
BCR thereby biasing signaling towards inhibitory signaling. For example, CD22 interacts with
sialic acid residues on BCRs. When we compare anergic B cells with naïve B cells, we find that
Syk phosphoprylation is significantly reduced in anergic B cells compared to naïve B cells. In
contrast, CD22 phosphorylation and SHP-1 association is relatively normal, consistent with a
bias towards inhibitory signaling. Finally, we have evidence that suggests that
monophosphorylated CD79A at the Y182 residue can directly recruit SHIP-1 to the BCR to
promote its phosphorylation. A manuscript describing these findings is in preparation, and we are
currently testing these hypotheses in mice that are restricted in their ability to phosphorylate
CD79A ITAMs. While these studies are beyond the scope of this manuscript, we have expanded
our discussion on how Lyn may operate to maintain tolerance.
